newsitem.title: UK: Britain gives Dominion's East Midlands bid go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Britain gives Dominion's East Midlands bid go-ahead.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday cleared the way for the takeover of regional electricity company East Midlands Electricity by U.S. power giant Dominion Resources Inc.

Ian Lang, trade and industry minister said he had decided not to refer the $2.15 billion agreed buy of East Midlands by Dominion's subsidiary DR Investments (UK) Plc to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
He said the decision was in line with his general approach to mergers involving regional electricity companies.
Lang's announcement follows his decision last week to give the go-ahead to CE Electric's 782 million pound ($1.3 billion) hostile bid for Northern Electric.
In addition to competition issues, Lang said he had also examined whether other public interest issues were raised by the bid but had decided there were no concerns warranting reference to the MMC.

He said DR Investments had given assurances to address regulatory concerns. These included ensuring sufficient resources for East Midlands to continue with its statutory and licence obligations and measures to ensure financial separation and independence for East Midlands.
Dominion said earlier this week that it had won acceptances representing 32.8 percent of East Midlands.
